title: Density-matched rejection initialisation
spec: In _solve_once, when x0 is None, draw centres not uniformly but by rejection sampling against a density that is low near existing centres. For each new centre, draw 30 uniform candidates in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 and keep the one whose distance to the nearest already-placed centre is largest (a best-candidate step). This is a cheap spread-out start. Keep the radii initialised at INIT_RADIUS and leave the SLSQP call and repair unchanged. Use only the seeded rng.

title: Site-occupancy annealing on a candidate grid
spec: Add a discrete pre-stage that is used only for the very first start. Build a 30 by 30 grid of candidate centres inside [0.05, 0.95]^2 and a fixed set of radius levels. Start with n occupied sites chosen at random. Run simulated annealing for about 3000 moves: each move relocates one occupied site to a random empty site, and the score is the sum of greedy radii, where each occupied site's radius is min(wall distance, half the distance to its nearest occupied neighbour). Accept with the Metropolis rule at a temperature that falls linearly from 0.01 to 0. Feed the best occupancy's centres and greedy radii into SLSQP as x0. The rest of the solver stays unchanged.

title: Frozen-core perturbation stage
spec: In each basin-hopping step, take the 25 percent largest-radius circles of the incumbent and hold their centres fixed while the rest are perturbed and solved with SLSQP, using a reduced problem over the other circles with the fixed ones included as constants in the pair constraints. Then run one full SLSQP over all circles from that result, accepting it only if its repaired sum improves the incumbent. This focuses the search on the loose part of the packing.

title: Rattler-aware relocation weights
spec: Within _relocate, weight the smallest circle's candidate score by the number of contacts it would make, counting a contact as a neighbour within 1e-3 of touching, and add a bonus of 0.5 times that count to the score. Draw the candidate centre from a random point that lies in the largest empty region found from 200 uniform samples, using the existing trials loop. This favours moves that place the smallest circle where it wedges between existing ones.

title: Tabu-protected relocation
spec: Modify _relocate so it avoids moving circles that were relocated in the last 5 basin-hopping steps. Maintain a deque of recently moved indices and exclude them from the candidate set when choosing k = argmin(r). If all small circles are tabu, pick the smallest non-tabu circle instead. Also, when a step is rejected (the new packing does not beat the incumbent), record the moved index in the tabu list anyway so the search keeps cycling through different circles. Keep the rest of the loop unchanged.

title: Breathing move: shrink then regrow
spec: Add a new basin-hopping move with probability 0.2 per step. Multiply all incumbent radii by a factor 0.97 and keep centres unchanged. Run _solve_once from this shrunken state (radii start small so SLSQP has room to move the centres apart). Then apply the usual repair. The move lets the packing loosen and reorganise around a fixed set of contact points, without the large centre jitter used by the current step. Only the move choice changes; the acceptance rule stays as it is.

title: Two-stage screening of basin-hopping candidates
spec: For each basin-hopping step, run a cheap SLSQP with maxiter 25 from the perturbed start and compute its repaired sum of radii. Only if that screened sum is within 0.01 of the incumbent's sum, run the full SLSQP with MAX_ITER 200 from the same start and accept it if it improves the incumbent. This spends the 30 s budget on more candidates, with the expensive solve reserved for plausible ones.

title: Adaptive operator selection over perturbation moves
spec: Define four basin-hopping moves: Gaussian kick (sigma 0.02), relocate-smallest (existing _relocate), a local cluster shake of five neighbouring circles, and a wall-slide that moves one boundary circle along its wall by U[-0.1,0.1]. Keep a success score per move, initialised at 1. Choose the move each step with probability proportional to its score plus 0.2 as an exploration floor. After each step, add 1 to the score of the move if it improved the incumbent and multiply all scores by 0.99 to forget old results. Log nothing and keep the code under 25 added lines.

title: Novelty-archive restart selection
spec: Maintain an archive of distinct local optima found during the run. After each SLSQP and repair, compute a fingerprint of the packing: the sorted radii rounded to 0.01 together with the sorted list of contact counts. Store the packing if its fingerprint is new. Each basin-hopping step, with probability 0.3, start from a random archive member chosen with probability proportional to its novelty (distance in sorted-radius space to the nearest other member) rather than from the incumbent. Keep the incumbent logic as it is otherwise, so the archive only changes which parent is perturbed.

title: Cluster-centred initialisation
spec: Replace the uniform random first-start centres in _solve_once with a clustered start. Draw k = round(sqrt(n)) cluster centres uniformly in [0.15, 0.85]^2, assign each circle to a cluster at random with probability proportional to a Dirichlet(1) weight, and place each circle at its cluster centre plus N(0, 0.08) noise, clipped into [0.05, 0.95]. Dense clusters separated by gaps give SLSQP a different initial contact pattern than the uniform start, and the rest of the search stays the same.

title: LP polish of radii with fixed centres
spec: After SLSQP and clipping, freeze the centres and solve a linear program with scipy.optimize.linprog that maximises the sum of radii subject to linearised non-overlap constraints r_i + r_j <= d_ij (using current distances) and wall bounds r_i <= the distance to each wall. Iterate the LP a few times, re-linearising at the new centres, then apply the existing repair. This replaces the crude shrink step with an optimal radius assignment.

title: Contact-count-scaled perturbation noise
spec: In the basin-hopping kick, scale the Gaussian noise per circle by its contact count instead of using a uniform sigma. Compute contacts from the incumbent as pairs with centre distance less than r_i + r_j + 1e-3, plus wall contacts where any side is within 1e-3 of the wall. Set sigma_i = 0.03 for circles with 0 or 1 contacts (likely rattlers, which should move freely) and sigma_i = 0.01 for circles with 4 or more contacts (rigid core, which should move little). Use 0.02 otherwise. Apply the same per-circle sigma to the radius noise. Everything else in the loop stays the same.

title: Lloyd centroidal relaxation kick
spec: Add a new perturbation applied before the SLSQP solve in the basin-hopping loop. Sample 4000 random points in the unit square and assign each to the nearest centre under the power (radically weighted) distance d(p,c_i)^2 - r_i^2. Move each centre to the centroid of its assigned points, blended with its current position at weight 0.5, for 3 iterations. This pushes the packing toward a power-diagram centroidal state and removes local bias before the SLSQP solve. Apply this move with probability 0.3 per step, otherwise use the existing kick. Seed the sampling from the rng argument.

title: Differential evolution over centres with SLSQP polish
spec: Replace the random multi-start with a population-based search. Keep a population of 40 candidate packings encoded as 3n-vectors (centres plus radii). Each generation, form a trial vector with DE/rand/1/bin (F=0.6, CR=0.9) and score it by a penalised objective: sum of radii after the greedy repair of _repair. Keep the top 8 members after each generation and polish only the best candidate with _solve_once as a warm start. Loop until 80 percent of the CPU budget is used, then return the best polished packing. Vectorise the repair and scoring over the population where possible so that a generation takes well under 0.1 s for n=32.

title: Final tight polish of the incumbent
spec: After the time loop in solve, take only the final best centres and radii and run one extra SLSQP call from them with maxiter 1000 and options ftol 1e-12 (passing the same pair and wall constraints). Keep the result only if the repaired sum of radii is larger than before. This is a single extra call that uses the time reserved by the 0.8 fraction, so lower TIME_FRACTION to 0.85 to keep the total under 30 s of CPU time.

title: Penalty least-squares with annealed radius weight
spec: Use scipy.optimize.least_squares (trust-region reflective, method='trf') instead of SLSQP for a stage of each solve. Residuals are the pairwise overlap violations, the wall violations, and a term -sqrt(w) * r_i for every circle, with w annealed from 0.01 to 1 across the stage. Variables are centres and radii. Finish with a short SLSQP polish on the active set. The least-squares solver handles the sparse residual structure differently from SLSQP's quadratic subproblems and may reach different local optima.

title: Sequential LP trust-region polish
spec: Replace the SLSQP call inside _solve_once with a sequential linear programming loop. At each iterate (c, r), linearise every pair-distance constraint, the wall constraints and the radius bounds, then solve the LP max sum(dr) using scipy.optimize.linprog(method='highs') over the step (dc, dr) with box trust-region bounds |dc|, |dr| <= delta. Accept the step if the true constraint violation shrinks and the objective rises, otherwise halve delta. Stop when delta < 1e-7 or after 60 iterations. Restrict the pair constraints to pairs closer than 2*(r_i+r_j)+0.1 to keep the LP small. The LP vertex solutions should land exactly on the active contacts, which SLSQP often leaves slightly loose. Keep the basin-hopping loop and _repair unchanged.

title: Thompson-sampled kick scale
spec: Replace the fixed 0.02 Gaussian kick in basin hopping with a choice among four kick scales {0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05}. Keep a Beta(successes+1, failures+1) posterior for each scale, where a success means the repaired candidate sum beats the incumbent. Each step draw one sample from each posterior with rng, use the scale with the largest sample, and update its counts after the solve. This is a bandit over step sizes; no schedule is assumed.

title: Quadrant domain-decomposition moves
spec: Add a move type to basin hopping. With probability 0.5, split the square into four quadrants around a random point (cx, cy) drawn in [0.35, 0.65]^2. Pick one quadrant at random. Take the circles whose centres lie inside it and solve a sub-problem with SLSQP on just those circles, keeping the other circles fixed as obstacles (add their non-overlap constraints as constants in the constraint function). Accept the sub-solution into the full configuration if the total radius sum improves after repair. Otherwise fall back to the existing full-SLSQP perturbation step.

title: One-fifth-rule adaptive perturbation size
spec: Track the success rate of basin-hopping steps over a sliding window of 20 steps. Start the Gaussian perturbation sigma at 0.02. Every 20 steps, multiply sigma by 1.2 if more than 1/5 of the steps improved the incumbent, and by 0.85 otherwise. Clamp sigma to [0.001, 0.1]. Apply the same sigma to both centre and radius noise. This replaces any fixed noise scale and needs no time-based schedule.

title: Swap radii of mismatched circles
spec: From the best packing, pick two circles whose radii differ by more than 0.05 and swap their radii while keeping their centres, then re-run SLSQP from that state. Repeat with random pairs for a fixed number of attempts per restart. Swapping radii changes which positions host large circles, a move that random perturbation rarely produces.

title: Soft-mode Hessian perturbation kick
spec: In the basin-hopping step, instead of isotropic Gaussian noise on the incumbent, build the Hessian of a penalty energy E(c,r) = -sum(r) + mu * sum(max(0, overlap)^2 + max(0, wall violation)^2) at the incumbent, using finite differences of the analytic gradient or a numerical Hessian (dimension 3n = 96, cheap). Take the eigenvectors with the 5 smallest non-zero eigenvalues (the floppy modes) and displace the incumbent along a random combination of them with amplitude drawn from U[0.01, 0.05], then clip to the square. Use the Gaussian kick with probability 0.5 and this soft-mode kick otherwise. Pass the perturbed point to _solve_once as the warm start, with everything else unchanged.

title: Path relinking between elite packings
spec: Keep the best two distinct packings found so far, and every 10 steps run a relinking step. Pick a random mixing parameter t in (0.2, 0.8), set the starting centres to (1-t)*A + t*B, where A and B are the centres of the two elites matched by nearest-index permutation after sorting by x coordinate, and set starting radii to the mean of the two radii. Run SLSQP from this start and keep the result only if it beats the incumbent. The step lies between two good basins, so it can find a new one without restarting from random points.

title: Axis-only coordinate kick
spec: Add a basin-hopping move that perturbs only one coordinate axis. With probability 0.3 per step, pick either x or y at random and add N(0, 0.03) noise to that coordinate for a random 30 percent subset of circles, leaving the other coordinate unchanged. Axis-aligned moves change which circles are in contact without disturbing the row structure of the packing in the other direction. Use the rng seed for all draws, and run the usual relocation and SLSQP afterwards.

title: Stagnation-triggered fresh restart
spec: Keep the basin-hopping loop, but count consecutive steps without improvement of best. If the count reaches K=25 (sum of radii not improved by more than 1e-6), discard the incumbent and restart from a fresh random SLSQP solve from _solve_once(n, rng), storing it as the new incumbent only if it is better than the old best. Otherwise continue basin hopping from the current best. Reset the counter after any restart or improvement. Use the same time check and repair step as now.

title: Feasibility bisection on a common radius
spec: Treat the packing as a decision problem. Bisect on a common radius r. For each r, minimise a penalty energy over centres only: the sum of squared overlap violations between pairs (max(0, 2r - d_ij)) plus squared wall violations, using L-BFGS-B with analytic gradients and a few random restarts seeded from rng. Take the largest r that reaches zero energy (within 1e-9), then use those centres as the x0 for the existing SLSQP call with radii set to r. Keep the existing basin-hopping loop and the repair step unchanged. This is a different route to the same local optima, which may land in different basins than radius-sum SLSQP.

title: Nearest-neighbour gap radii for the basin-hopping start
spec: In solve, after the first _solve_once, replace the radius perturbation r0 = br + N(0, 0.02) by a gap-based initialisation for each perturbed centre set: for every circle compute the distance to its nearest other centre and to the four walls, set r_i = 0.5 * min(nearest-neighbour distance, 2 * wall distance) * U(0.8, 1.0) with the same rng, then pass these as the radii to _relocate and _solve_once. Use this only on a random half of the basin-hopping steps, so the incumbent's radii still get used otherwise.

title: Elite memetic recombination
spec: Maintain an elite pool of the best 5 packings found so far, deduplicated by sorted radii. Each new start is either a fresh random init (probability 0.3) or a child made by taking the centres of one elite parent for the circles in one half of the square and the centres of another parent for the other half, then fixing the circle count by moving surplus circles to random positions. Run SLSQP on each child and insert the result into the pool.

title: Elite-density sampled starts
spec: Maintain a small elite set of the top 5 distinct packings found so far. For each new start, pick one elite packing at random, then sample a fresh centre set by taking each elite centre and adding Gaussian noise with a standard deviation equal to 0.3 times the mean nearest-neighbour distance, then clip to the square. Radii start from the elite radii shifted by the same noise. This is an estimation-of-distribution step over packing structure rather than a pure kick on the incumbent, and it fills the role of the first random start once the elite set has at least two members. Use the seed for every draw.

title: Symmetry-reduced search
spec: Optimise under a prescribed symmetry, then unfold. Pick one symmetry at random per call from {reflection in the diagonal x=y, 180-degree rotation about (0.5,0.5)}, seeded by rng. Parameterise only ceil(n/2) free circles plus their images, with the self-symmetric circles (on the axis or centre) handled by fixing them to the symmetry set. Run SLSQP on the reduced variables (about half the constraints), which is much faster and explores a different region. Then unfold to all n circles, run one unconstrained SLSQP polish from that configuration, and keep the best of the symmetric and polished results in the basin-hopping loop.

title: Row-strip layout start
spec: In _solve_once, when x0 is None, replace the uniform random centres with a row-based layout. Draw k uniformly from {4,5,6,7}, split n circles into k rows with random counts that sum to n, and place each row at a height evenly spaced in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]. Within a row, space centres evenly along x with small uniform jitter (about 0.02) and a random horizontal offset per row. Set initial radii to about 0.4 times the row spacing. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged. Use rng for every draw so the seed still controls the run.

title: Successive-halving over starts
spec: Allocate the time budget across many starts in rounds. Round 1 draws 40 random starts and runs SLSQP with maxiter=25 on each, keeping the top 10 by sum of repaired radii. Round 2 runs maxiter=80 on the top 10 and keeps the top 3. Round 3 gives the top 3 the full MAX_ITER budget and then uses the remaining time for basin hopping from the best. Stop each stage by the process-time clock so the total stays within TIME_FRACTION. This replaces the fixed-budget random restarts with a bracket that spends most compute on promising basins.

title: Hooke spring relaxation start
spec: Replace the random first start with a force-directed relaxation. Place circles uniformly at random in the square. Give every pair a spring with rest length equal to 1.6 times the sum of their current radii, which start at 0.06, and a soft wall repulsion. Run 400 gradient steps of overdamped motion with a step size that cools linearly to zero. Radii then grow each step toward the local clearance, capped at the wall and neighbour gaps. Finally pass centres and radii to SLSQP as x0. This is a physical start, not a grid.

title: Two-timescale kick scale with stagnation counter
spec: Keep two perturbation scales, a fast scale of 0.02 and a slow scale of 0.005, and choose between them by a rolling success count over the last 10 steps. When the fast scale has produced no improvement in 10 consecutive steps, switch the next 10 steps to the slow scale, and switch back on any improvement. Only the choice of sigma changes; the SLSQP, relocation and repair steps stay the same. This is a schedule over the kick magnitude, separate from the annealed and Thompson-sampled variants already tried, and it needs only a counter and two constants.

title: Quadrant-split coarse-to-fine start
spec: Build the first layout by splitting the square into a 2 by 2 grid of quadrants. Assign circles to quadrants in proportion to a random split of n. Solve each quadrant as a small packing scaled into its cell using a short SLSQP run, with the cell as the square, then stitch the four results into the full square and run SLSQP on all circles with the stitched centres as x0. Repair then runs as normal. This is coarse-to-fine decomposition at the level of the whole start, and it gives the global optimiser structure at quadrant scale.

title: Greedy radius inflation sweep after repair
spec: After _repair, add a deterministic growth pass. Repeat up to 5 sweeps: for each circle in random order, compute the largest radius it can take without overlapping any other circle or leaving the square, which is min over neighbours of (d_ij - r_j) and over the walls, and set its radius to that value if larger. The repair only shrinks radii, so this pass can recover slack left by the SLSQP tolerance and by the repair, with a feasibility check at the end. Apply it to every candidate before comparing sums of radii.

title: Phantom-circle density start
spec: In _solve_once with no x0, solve first with n+3 circles in the optimisation, where the last 3 are phantoms. Phantoms are present in all pair and wall constraints but carry zero weight in the objective, so they only push neighbours apart and absorb space. After the solve, delete the phantoms, keep the n largest-radius circles, and run SLSQP again on the n-circle problem from that state. Sum radii are computed only over the real circles. This is a different use of the spare-circle idea from growing or shrinking the count.

title: Procrustes consensus crossover of elite packings
spec: Keep the top four distinct packings from the search. For a new start, take two of them at random, apply each of the 8 symmetries of the unit square to the second, and match circles to the first by minimum total centre distance with scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment. Average the matched centres and radii, then use the averaged configuration as the x0 of one SLSQP solve (with a small jitter from rng). Keep the current basin hopping for the other steps. This recombines structure across elite packings instead of perturbing a single one.

title: Epoch culling of independent chains
spec: Replace the single basin-hopping chain with a population of 6 independent chains, each started from its own _solve_once result with a different rng child stream (use rng.spawn or distinct seeds derived from the seed argument). Split the time budget into 4 epochs of equal CPU time. At the end of each epoch rank the chains by repaired radius sum, drop the worst 3, and clone the best 3 with their incumbent copied in. Run basin-hopping steps within each chain as before. Return the best chain at the end. Use only seeded randomness. The point is to spend budget on the chains that are doing well instead of spreading it evenly across restarts.
